The following are equivalent \begin{enumerate} \item there exists a cartesian diagram $$ \xymatrix{ X \ar[r] \ar[d] & X_0 \ar[d] \\ S \ar[r] & S_0 } $$ where $X_0 \to S_0$ is a finite type morphism of Noetherian schemes and $\alpha_0 \in z(X_0/S_0, r)$ such that $\alpha$ is the base change of $\alpha_0$ by $S \to S_0$ \item there exists a completely decomposed proper morphism $g : S' \to S$ of finite…

title: more-etale-remark-shriek-to-star
snippet: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a finite type separated morphism of schemes with $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Below we will construct a map $$ Rf_!K \longrightarrow Rf_*K $$ functorial for $K$ in $D^+_{tors}(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ or $D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ if $\Lambda$ is torsion. This transformation of functors in both cases is compatible with \begin{enumerate} \item the isomorphism $Rg_! \circ Rf_! \to R(g \circ f)_!$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-shriek-composition} and the isomorphism $Rg_* \circ Rf_* \to R(g \circ f)_*$ of Cohomology on Sites, Lemma…

title: sites-lemma-isomorphism-sheafifications
snippet: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map of presheaves of sets on $\mathcal{C}$. Denote $\mathcal{B}$ the set of $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ such that $\mathcal{F}(U) \to \mathcal{G}(U)$ is bijective. If every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering by elements of $\mathcal{B}$, then $\mathcal{F}^\# \to \mathcal{G}^\#$ is an isomorphism.

title: sites-example-not-equivalent
snippet: Let $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be sites. Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ and $v : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be functors of the underlying categories such that $v$ is right adjoint to $u$. Lemma \ref{lemma-continuous-with-continuous-left-adjoint} shows that if $v$ is continuous, then $u$ is cocontinous. Conversely, if $u$ is cocontinuous, then we can't conclude that $v$ is continuous. We will give an example of this phenomenon using the big \'etale and smooth sites of a scheme, but presumably there is an elementary example as well.

title: algebra-example-not-local
snippet: If $R$ is a local ring and $\mathfrak p \subset R$ is a non-maximal prime ideal, then $R \to R_\mathfrak p$ is not a local homomorphism.

title: algebra-lemma-mini-separability
snippet: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 1$. Let $K/k$ be a field extension generated by $x_1, \ldots, x_{n + 1} \in K$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}$ is a transcendence base of $K/k$, \item for every $k$-linearly independent subset $\{a_1, \ldots, a_m\}$ of $K$ the set $\{a^p_1, \ldots, a_m^p\}$ is $k$-linearly independent. \end{enumerate} Then there is $1 \leq j \leq n+1$ such that $\{ x_1, \ldots, \widehat{x}_j, \ldots, x_{n+1}\}$ is a separating transcendence base for $K / k$.

title: derived-remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations
snippet: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $K^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{A}$. Then $\tau_{\geq -n}K^\bullet$ is an inverse system of complexes and which in particular determines an inverse system in $D(\mathcal{A})$. Let us assume that $R\lim \tau_{\geq -n}K^\bullet$ exists. Then the canonical maps $c_n : K^\bullet \to \tau_{\geq -n}K^\bullet$ are compatible with the transition maps of our inverse system.

title: more-algebra-example-laurent
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring and let $I, J\subset R$ be ideals. Then $\text{Fit}_0(R/I) = I$, $\text{Fit}_0(R/I \oplus R/J) = IJ$, $\text{Fit}_1(R/I\oplus R/J) = I+J$.

title: more-algebra-lemma-lift-smooth-henselian
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring and $S$ a smooth $R$-algebra. Assume that $A$ is an $R$-algebra and $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair. Then any $R$-algebra map $S \to A/I$ can be lifted to an $R$-algebra map $S \to A$.

title: more-algebra-lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent
snippet: Let $R' \to R$ be a surjective ring map whose kernel is a nilpotent ideal. Let $K' \in D(R')$ and set $K = K' \otimes_{R'}^\mathbf{L} R$. Let $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$. Then $K$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$ if and only if $K'$ does.

title: more-algebra-lemma-check-pseudo-coherent-modulo-nilpotent
snippet: Let $R' \to R$ be a surjective ring map whose kernel is a nilpotent ideal. Let $K' \in D(R')$ and set $K = K' \otimes_{R'}^\mathbf{L} R$. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent if and only if $K'$ is pseudo-coherent.

title: more-algebra-lemma-H0-Can-adjoint
snippet: In Remark \ref{remark-glueing-data} the functor $H^0 : \text{Glue}(R \to S, f_1, \ldots, f_t) \to \text{Mod}_R$ is a right adjoint to the functor $\text{Can} : \text{Mod}_R \to \text{Glue}(R \to S, f_1, \ldots, f_t)$.

title: modules-remark-pullback-s-open
snippet: Given a morphism of locally ringed spaces $f : Y \to X$ (see Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-locally-ringed-space}) the inverse image $f^{-1}(X_s)$ is equal to $Y_{f^*s}$, where $f^*s \in \Gamma(Y, f^*\mathcal{L})$ is the pullback of $s$.

title: modules-lemma-triangle-differentials
snippet: Let $f : X \to Y$, $g : Y \to S$ be morphisms of ringed spaces Then there is a canonical exact sequence $$ f^*\Omega_{Y/S} \to \Omega_{X/S} \to \Omega_{X/Y} \to 0 $$ where the maps come from applications of Lemma \ref{lemma-functoriality-differentials-ringed-spaces}.

title: cohomology-lemma-higher-direct-image-colimit
snippet: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces. Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ be a system of abelian sheaves on $X$. Set $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$. Let $p \geq 0$ be an integer. Assume the set of opens $V \subset Y$ such that $H^p(f^{-1}(V), \mathcal{F}) = \colim H^p(f^{-1}(V), \mathcal{F}_i)$ is a basis for the topology on $Y$. Then $R^pf_*\mathcal{F} = \colim R^pf_*\mathcal{F}_i$.

title: sites-cohomology-lemma-higher-direct-image-colimit
snippet: Let $f : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a morphism of sites corresponding to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$. Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ be a system of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$. Set $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$. Let $p \geq 0$ be an integer. Denote $\mathcal{B}$ the set of $V \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ such that $H^p(u(V), \mathcal{F}) = \colim H^p(u(V), \mathcal{F}_i)$. If every object of $\mathcal{D}$ has a covering by elements of $\mathcal{B}$, then $R^pf_*\mathcal{F} = \colim R^pf_*\mathcal{F}_i$.

title: properties-lemma-isolated-dim-0-locally-noetherian
snippet: Let $x$ be a point of a locally Noetherian scheme $X$. Then $\dim_x(X) = 0$ if and only if $x$ is an isolated point of $X$.

title: morphisms-lemma-normalization-trivial
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme with locally finitely many irreducible components. The normalization morphism $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ is an isomorphism if and only if $X$ is normal.

title: topologies-example-not-fpqc
snippet: Let $X = X_1 \cup X_2$ where $X_1 = X_2 = \Spec(k[t_1,t_2,\dots])$ be the non-quasi-separated scheme from Schemes, Example \ref{schemes-example-not-quasi-separated}, and $Y = X_1 \amalg \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X_2, 0})$. Then the obvious morphism $f : Y \to X$ is flat and surjective, and (since $Y$ is quasi-compact) trivially satisfies (4) of Lemma \ref{lemma-recognize-fpqc-covering}. But $\{f : Y \to X\}$ isn't an fpqc covering. Namely, we claim there is no quasi-compact open $W$ of $Y$ whose image by $f$ is $X_2$. Namely, $f^{-1}(X_2) = X_1 \setminus \{0\} \amalg \Spec(\mathcal{O}_{X_2, 0})$.

title: examples-lemma-nonsplit-locally-split
snippet: There exists a ring $R$ and a nonsplit sequence of modules which becomes split Zariski locally.

title: sheaves-lemma-characterize-epi-mono
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. \begin{enumerate} \item Epimorphisms (resp.\ monomorphisms) in the category of presheaves are exactly the surjective (resp.\ injective) maps of presheaves. \item Epimorphisms (resp.\ monomorphisms) in the category of sheaves are exactly the surjective (resp.\ injective) maps of sheaves, and are exactly those maps which are surjective (resp.\ injective) on all the stalks. \end{enumerate}

title: sheaves-lemma-sheafify-epi-mono
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. The sheafification of a surjective (resp.\ injective) morphism of presheaves of sets is surjective (resp.\ injective).

title: sites-example-constant-sheaf
snippet: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $E$ be a set. The {\it constant sheaf $\underline{E}$ with value $E$} is the sheafification of the presheaf given by the constant functor with value $E$. It is characterized by the rule $\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\underline{E}, \mathcal{F}) = \Mor_{\textit{Sets}}(E, \Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}))$ for every sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$ where the notation is from Definition \ref{definition-global-sections}.

title: fields-lemma-common-extension-field
snippet: Let $k$ be a field and let $E/k$ and $F/k$ be field extensions. Then there exists a common field extension $M/k$, i.e., an extension field such that there exist maps $E \to M$ and $F \to M$ of extensions of $k$.

title: algebra-lemma-intersection-not-zero
snippet: Let $A \subset B$ be an inclusion of domains inducing an algebraic extension of fraction fields. If $J \subset B$ is a nonzero ideal, then $A \cap J$ is nonzero too. Thus the image of a proper closed subset of $\Spec(B)$ is not dense in $\Spec(A)$.

title: algebra-lemma-projective-modulo-two-ideals
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I, J \subset R$ be ideals such that $I \cap J = 0$. Let $P$ be an $R$-module such that $P/IP$ is a projective $R/I$-module and $P/JP$ is a projective $R/J$-module. Then $P$ is a projective $R$-module.

title: algebra-lemma-flatness-scallop
snippet: Let $A$ be a ring, let $M$ be an $A$-module, and let $f \in A$. If \begin{enumerate} \item $f$ is a nonzerodivisor on $A$ and $M$, \item $M_f$ is a flat $A_f$-module, and \item $M/fM$ is a flat $A/fA$-module, \end{enumerate} Then $M$ is a flat $A$-module. Same with ``flat'' replaced by ``faithfully flat''.

title: algebra-lemma-flatness-scallop-pre
snippet: Let $A$ be a ring, let $M$ be an $A$-module. Let $I = (f_1, \ldots, f_r)$ be an ideal of $A$ generated by $r \geq 1$ elements. If \begin{enumerate} \item $M_{f_i}$ is a flat $A_{f_i}$-module for $i = 1, \ldots, r$, \item $M/IM$ is a flat $A/I$-module, \item $\text{Tor}_i^A(M, A/I) = 0$ for $i = 1, \ldots, r + 1$. \end{enumerate} Then $M$ is a flat $A$-module. Same with ``flat'' replaced by ``faithfully flat''.

title: more-algebra-lemma-CRT-henselization
snippet: Let $I_1, I_2, \dots, I_n \subset A$ be ideals in a ring $A$. Suppose $I_i + I_j = A$ for $i \not = j$, $1 \leq i, j \leq n$. Denote $A^h$ the henselization of the pair $(A, I_1 \cap \ldots \cap I_n)$ and $A_i^h$ the henselization of the pair $(A, I_i)$. Then the natural morphism $$ A^h \to \prod\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} A^h_i $$ is an isomorphism.

title: more-algebra-lemma-descent-projective-injective-finite-Noetherian-rings
snippet: Let $R \to S$ be a finite injective homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Let $P$ be an $R$-module. If $P \otimes_R S$ is a projective $S$-module, then $P$ is a projective $R$-module.

title: more-algebra-lemma-regular-goes-up
snippet: Let $\varphi : R \to S$ be a ring map. Assume \begin{enumerate} \item $\varphi$ is regular, \item $S$ is Noetherian, and \item $R$ is Noetherian and regular. \end{enumerate} Then $S$ is regular.

title: more-algebra-lemma-CM-goes-up
snippet: Let $\varphi : R \to S$ be a ring map. Assume \begin{enumerate} \item $\varphi$ is regular, \item $S$ is Noetherian, and \item $R$ is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay. \end{enumerate} Then $S$ is Cohen-Macaulay.

title: more-algebra-theorem-fs-regular
snippet: [Andr\'e] Let $A \to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let $k$ be the residue field of $A$ and $\overline{B} = B \otimes_A k$ the special fibre. Assume $A \to A^\wedge$ is regular\footnote{For example, if $A$ is a G-ring or (quasi-)excellent, see Sections \ref{section-G-ring} and \ref{section-excellent}.}.

title: more-algebra-lemma-kunneth-converges
snippet: Under the assumptions above, if in addition \begin{enumerate} \item the filtration on $K^\bullet$ is finite and the filtration on $L^\bullet$ is finite, or \item more generally the following are true \begin{enumerate} \item $F^iK^\bullet$ is acyclic for $i \gg 0$, \item $F^iK^\bullet \to K^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism for $i \ll 0$, \item $F^jL^\bullet$ is acyclic for $j \gg 0$, and \item $F^jL^\bullet \to L^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism for $j \ll 0$.

title: more-algebra-lemma-resolution-filtered-complex
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $K^\bullet$ be a filtered complex. There exists a map $f : P^\bullet \to K^\bullet$ of filtered complexes such that \begin{enumerate} \item each $P^n$, $F^iP^n$, $\text{gr}^iP^n$ is a free $R$-module, \item the complexes of $R$-modules $P^\bullet$, $F^iP^\bullet$, and $\text{gr}^iP^\bullet$ are K-flat, \item $f$ induces quasi-isomorphisms $P^\bullet \to K^\bullet$, $F^iP^\bullet \to F^iK^\bullet$, and $\text{gr}^iP^\bullet \to \text{gr}^iK^\bullet$. \end{enumerate}

title: more-algebra-proposition-kunneth-filtered
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $K^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$ be filtered complexes of $R$-modules. Then there exists a filtered complex $T^\bullet$ representing $K^\bullet \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} L^\bullet$ in $D(R)$ such that the associated spectral sequence has $E_1$-page $$ E_1^{p, q} = \bigoplus\nolimits_{i + j = p} H^{p + q}(\text{gr}^iK^\bullet \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} \text{gr}^jL^\bullet) $$ If \begin{enumerate} \item $F^iK^\bullet$ is acyclic for $i \gg 0$, \item $F^iK^\bullet \to K^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism for $i \ll 0$, \item $F^jL^\bullet$ is acyclic for $j \gg 0$, and \item $F^jL^\bullet…

title: more-algebra-lemma-kunneth-spectral-sequence
snippet: [K\"unneth Spectral Sequence] Let $R$ be a ring. Let $K$ and $L$ be objects of $D^b(R)$. There exists a bigraded bounded spectral sequence $\{E_r\}_{r \geq 2}$ with $$ E_2^{p, q} = \bigoplus\nolimits_{i + j = q} \text{Tor}^R_{-p}(H^i(K), H^j(L)) $$ and $d_r$ of bidegree $(r, -r + 1)$ converging to $H^{p + q}(K \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} L)$.

title: more-algebra-example-kunneth-dedekind
snippet: If $R = \mathbf{Z}$ or more generally if $R$ is a Dedekind domain, then $\text{Tor}_i^R(M, N) = 0$ for $i \not \in \{0, 1\}$ for all $R$-modules $M$ and $N$. Hence the spectral sequence of Lemma \ref{lemma-kunneth-spectral-sequence} degenerates at the $E_2$ page and we get short exact sequences $$ 0 \to \bigoplus_{i + j = n} H^i(K) \otimes_R H^j(L) \to H^n(K \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} L) \to \bigoplus_{i + j = n + 1} \text{Tor}^R_1(H^i(K), H^j(L)) \to 0 $$ for all $n \in \mathbf{Z}$.

title: more-algebra-remark-dual-perfect-complex
snippet: Let $A$ be a ring. Let $K \in D(A)$ be perfect. If $K$ has tor-amplitude in $[a, b]$ then its dual $K^\vee$ has tor-amplitude in $[-b, -a]$. This follows from the last statement in Lemma \ref{lemma-perfect} and the description of $K^\vee$ in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma-dual-perfect-complex}.

title: more-algebra-lemma-bounded-above-mod-I
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal. Let $K$ be an object of $D(R)$ such that $H^i(K \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} R/I) = 0$ for $i > 0$. Then \begin{enumerate} \item $H^i(K \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} R/I^n) = 0$ for all $n \geq 1$ and $i > 0$, \item $H^i(K \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} N) = 0$ for any $I$-power torsion $R$-module $N$ and $i > 0$, and \item for any $M \in D^b(R)$ whose cohomology modules $H^i(M)$ are $I$-power torsion and $0$ for $i > 0$ we have $H^i(K \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} M) = 0$ for $i > 0$. \end{enumerate}

title: more-algebra-lemma-derived-complete-bounded
snippet: Let $I = (f_1, \ldots, f_r)$ be a finitely generated ideal of a ring $A$. Let $K$ be a derived complete object of $D(A)$. The following are equivalent \begin{enumerate} \item $H^i(K) = 0$ for $i > 0$, \item $H^i(K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A/I) = 0$ for $i > 0$, \item $H^i(K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} K_1^\bullet) = 0$ for $i > 0$ where $K_1^\bullet$ is as in Situation \ref{situation-koszul}. \end{enumerate}

title: more-algebra-lemma-f-bounded
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring and $f \in R$. Let $M \in D(R)$ and let $C$ be the cone of $f : M \to M$. If $H^i(M)_f = 0$ for $i < 0$ and $H^i(C) = 0$ for $i < -1$, then $H^i(M) = 0$ for $i < 0$.

title: more-algebra-lemma-f-flat
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring and $f \in R$. Let $M \in D(R)$. Assume \begin{enumerate} \item $H^i(M) = 0$ for $i > 0$, \item $M \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} R_f$ is isomorphic to a flat $R_f$-module placed in degree $0$, \item $M \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} R/fR$ is isomorphic to a flat $R/fR$-module placed in degree $0$. \end{enumerate} Then $M$ is isomorphic to a flat $R$-module placed in degree $0$.

title: dpa-remark-pushout
snippet: Let $$ \xymatrix{ (B, J, \delta) \ar[r] & (B'', J'', \delta'') \\ (A, I, \gamma) \ar[r] \ar[u] & (B', J', \delta') \ar[u] } $$ be a pushout in the category of divided power rings (pushouts exist by Lemma \ref{lemma-colimits}). Then \begin{enumerate} \item $B''/J'' = B/J \otimes_{A/I} B'/J'$, \item the map $\varphi : B \otimes_A B' \to B''$ is surjective, and \item the map $J \otimes_A B' + B \otimes_A J' \to J''$ induced by $\varphi$ is surjective. \end{enumerate} To see (1) consider maps $(B'', J'', \delta'') \to (C, (0), \emptyset)$ and apply the definition of a pushout.

title: dpa-remark-ryo-suzuki
snippet: With $A \supset I$ as in Lemma \ref{lemma-need-only-gamma-p}, let $\delta : I \to I$ be a map satisfying (2) and (3) of the lemma. Then (1) holds too. First, we prove $\delta(nx) = n\delta(x) + \frac{n^p - n}{p!}x^p$ for $n \geq 1$ by induction on $n$. The case $n = 1$ is OK. Assume that it is OK for some $n$, then $\delta((n + 1)x) = \delta(nx) + \delta(x) + (\sum_{i = 1}^{p - 1} \frac{n^i}{i!(p - i)!})x^p = (n + 1)\delta(x) + \left( \frac{n^p - n}{p!} + \frac{(n + 1)^p}{p!} - \frac{n^p + 1}{p!} \right)x^p = (n + 1)\delta(x) + \frac{(n + 1)^p - (n + 1)}{p!}x^p$, so it is also OK for $n + 1$.

title: morphisms-lemma-quasi-coherence-scalar-restriction
snippet: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal{A}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-algebra. An $\mathcal{A}$-module is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal{O}_S$-module if and only if it is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal{A}$-module.

title: more-morphisms-lemma-flatness-criterion
snippet: [Longke Tang] Let $f : X \to S$ be a surjective morphism of finite presentation. Let $M$ be an object of $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S)$ such that $H^i(M) = 0$ for $i > 0$. The following are equivalent \begin{enumerate} \item $M$ is isomorphic to a flat $\mathcal{O}_S$-module placed in degree $0$, \item $Lf^*M$ is isomorphic to a flat $\mathcal{O}_X$-module placed in degree $0$. \end{enumerate}

title: intersection-lemma-projection-generically-immersion-refined
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space. Let $Z \subset X \subset \mathbf{P}(V)$ be closed subvarieties with $Z \not = X \not = \mathbf{P}(V)$. Let $x \in Z$ be a point which is nonsingular on $X$. Then there is a nonempty Zariski open $U \subset \mathbf{P}(V)$ such that for all closed points $p \in U$ the morphism $r_p|_Z : Z \to r_p(Z)$ is an isomorphism over an open neighbourhood of $r_p(x)$.

title: equiv-remark-matress
snippet: Let $X^0 \to X^1 \to X^2 \to X^0[1]$ and $Y^0 \to Y^1 \to Y^2 \to Y^0[1]$ be distinguished triangles in a triangulated category. For $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ write $p = 3n + i$ with $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ and set we set $X^p = X^i[n]$. Simlarly for $Y^q$. Consider the double complex with terms $$ K^{p, q} = \Hom(X^{-p}, Y^q) $$ The differential $d_1 : K^{p, q} \to K^{p + 1, q}$ is given by the map $X^{-p - 1} \to X^{-p}$ (equal to the corresponding map in the first distinguished triangle up the a shift) and the differential $d_2 : K^{p, q} \to K^{p, q + 1}$ likewise by the map $Y^q \to Y^{q + 1}$.

title: equiv-remark-dual-matress
snippet: Let $k$ be a field and let $K^{\bullet, \bullet}$ be a double complex of finite dimensional $k$-vector spaces which is also a matress as in Remark \ref{remark-matress}. We claim that the dual double complex $L^{p, q} = \Hom_k(K^{-q, -p}, k)$ is also a matress. The exactness of rows and columns and the 3-periodicity are immediate.

title: examples-remark-projective-with-dual-finite-not-finite
snippet: The example above where $R = \prod_{n \in \mathbf{N}} \mathbf{F}_2$ and $I$ the ideal generated by the idempotents $e_n = (1, 1, \ldots, 1, 0, \ldots )$ also gives us an example $M = I$ of a non-finitely generated projective module whose dual is finitely generated and even finite free. Namely, using the strategy in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma-ideal-generated-by-idempotents-projective} the reader shows that $\Hom_R(I, R) \cong R$.

title: examples-remark-torsors-over-regular
snippet: We can get rid of the $2$-dimensional condition on $W$ in Lemma \ref{lemma-torsors-over-two-dimensional-regular}. Namely, if $W$ is noetherian, regular and integral, then (1) $P(W)\to P(K)$ is bijective for every $G$-torsor $P$ and (2) $H^1(W,G)\to H^1(K,G)$ is injective. A sketch of the proof goes as follows. First (2) clearly follows from (1). For (1), the injectivity is trivial, and surjectivity (as in the current proof) is about proving that the schematic closure of a rational section is a section.

title: morphisms-lemma-open-base-change-dominant
snippet: Let $f : X \to S$ be a dominant morphism of schemes. Let $g : S' \to S$ be an open morphism of schemes, and let $f' : X' \to S'$ be the base change of $f$ by $g$. Then $f'$ is dominant.

title: varieties-lemma-geometrically-irreducible-self-product
snippet: A scheme $X$ over a field $k$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ if and only if $X\times_k X$ is irreducible.

title: descent-lemma-descending-property-dominant
snippet: The property $\mathcal{P}(f) =$``$f$ is quasi-compact and dominant'' is fpqc local on the base.

title: descent-lemma-descending-property-dominant-over-field
snippet: Let $E/k$ be a field extension. Then a morphism $X \to Y$ over $k$ is dominant if and only if the pullback $X_E \to Y_E$ is dominant.

title: descent-lemma-descending-fppf-property-dominant
snippet: The property $\mathcal{P}(f) =$``$f$ is dominant'' is fppf local on the base.

title: groupoids-lemma-descend-along-finite-with-bound
snippet: Let $X \to Y$ be a surjective finite locally free morphism. Let $d$ be a positive integer. Assume that for every geometric point $\bar{y} : \mathrm{Spec}(k) \to Y$ the fiber $X_{\bar{y}}$ has at most $d$ points. Let $V$ be a scheme over $X$ such that for all $(y, v_1, \ldots, v_d)$ where $y \in Y$ and $v_1, \ldots, v_d \in V_y$ there exists an affine open $U \subset V$ with $v_1, \ldots, v_d \in U$. Then any descent datum on $V/X/Y$ is effective.

title: groupoids-lemma-descend-along-finite-radicial
snippet: Let $X \to Y$ be a surjective finite locally free morphism which is radicial. Let $V$ be a scheme over $X$. Then any descent datum on $V/X/Y$ is effective.

title: formal-spaces-lemma-when-isomorphism
snippet: Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subspace and set $T = |Z|$. The canonical morphism $c : X^\wedge_Z \to X_{/T}$ is an isomorphism if $Z \to X$ is of finite presentation, but not in general.

title: exercises-exercise-definitions-spring-2025
snippet: [Definitions] Provide brief definitions of the italicized concepts. \begin{enumerate} \item a {\it scheme} $X$, \item a {\it quasi-coherent module} on a scheme $X$, \item the {\it Picard group} of a scheme $X$, \item give a morphism $f : X \to Y$ of schemes and an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$, the {\it pushforward} $f_*\mathcal{F}$, \item a {\it closed immersion} of schemes, and \item a {\it variety} over a given field $k$. \end{enumerate}

title: exercises-exercise-results-spring-2025
snippet: [Theorems] Precisely and succintly state one nontrivial fact discussed in the lectures related to each item (if there is more than one then just pick one of them). \begin{enumerate} \item the topological space of a scheme $X$, \item a representability criterion for functors on the category of schemes, \item the Picard functor for a smooth projective curve $X$ over an algebraically closed field $k$, \item torsion in the Picard group of a smooth projective curve $X$ over an algebraically closed field $k$, \item a theorem on the Picard group of a product $X \times Y \times Z$ of smooth…

title: exercises-exercise-affine-line-infinite-nr-points
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Explain why $\Spec(k[x])$ has infinitely many points.

title: exercises-exercise-hypersurface-variety
snippet: Let $k$ be a field and let $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ be variables. Let $f \in k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be a nonconstant polynomial. Let $X = \Spec(k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f))$. What property should $f$ have in order for $X$ to be a variety over $k$?

title: exercises-exercise-find-singular-point
snippet: Find a singular point (you do not need to find all of them) on the spectrum of $\mathbf{C}[x, y]/(x^5 - 5xy^4 + 20y - 16)$ viewed as a variety over $\mathbf{C}$.

title: exercises-exercise-kernel-restriction-pic-curve
snippet: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field $k$. Let $x \in X(k)$ be a closed point on $X$. Let $U = X \setminus \{x\}$. What can you say about the kernel of the restriction map $\Pic(X) \to \Pic(U)$?

title: exercises-exercise-sections-degree-2g-minus-4
snippet: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of genus $g \geq 100$. What values can $h^0(\mathcal{L}) = \dim_k H^0(X, \mathcal{L})$ take for $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of degree $2g - 4$ on $X$? Answer as completely as you can.

title: algebra-lemma-quasi-finite-above-p
snippet: Let $R \to S$ be a finite type ring map and $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $R$. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $R \to S$ is quasi-finite at all primes of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, \item $S \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finite $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra, and \item $\Spec(S \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p))$ is a finite set. \end{enumerate}

title: algebra-lemma-de-rham-complex-base-change
snippet: Suppose that we have ring maps $A \to A'$ and $A \to B$. Set $B' = B \otimes_A A'$, so that we obtain a diagram as above. Then the canonical map defined above induces an isomorphism $\Omega^\bullet_{B/A} \otimes_A A' = \Omega^\bullet_{B'/A'}$ of complexes.

title: algebra-lemma-principal-parts-base-change
snippet: Suppose that we have ring maps $A \to A'$ and $A \to B$ and a $B$-module $M$. Set $B' = B \otimes_A A'$ and view $M' = M \otimes_A A'$ as a $B'$-module. The map of Remark \ref{remark-functoriality-principal-parts} induces an isomorphism $P^k_{B/A}(M) \otimes_A A' = P^k_{B'/A'}(M')$.

title: algebra-lemma-principal-parts-diagonal
snippet: Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $M$ be an $S$-module. Let $J = \Ker(S \otimes_R S \to S)$ be the kernel of the multiplication map. There is a canonical isomorphism of $S$-modules $$ P^k_{S/R}(M) \longrightarrow (S \otimes_R M)/J^{k + 1}(S \otimes_R M) $$ where $s \in S$ acts on the target via multiplication by $s \otimes 1$ and such that the universal differential operators of order $k$ to the map given by $m \mapsto \text{class of }1 \otimes m$.

title: algebra-lemma-base-change-formally-unramified
snippet: Let $R \to S$ be a formally unramified map. Let $R \to R'$ be any ring map. Then the base change $S' = R' \otimes_R S$ is formally unramified over $R'$.

title: algebra-lemma-base-change-formally-etale
snippet: Let $R \to S$ be a formally \'etale map. Let $R \to R'$ be any ring map. Then the base change $S' = R' \otimes_R S$ is formally \'etale over $R'$.

title: algebra-lemma-formally-etale-omega
snippet: Let $R \to S \to S'$ be ring maps. Let $J$, resp.\ $J'$ be the kernel of the multiplication map $S \otimes_R S \to S$, resp.\ $S' \otimes_{R'} S' \to S'$. If $S \to S'$ is formally \'etale, then the map $$ S' \otimes_S \left((S \otimes_R S)/J^{k + 1}\right) \longrightarrow (S' \otimes_R S')/(J')^{k + 1} $$ is an isomorphism for all $k \geq 0$. In particular, the map $S' \otimes_S \Omega_{S/R} \to \Omega_{S'/R}$ is an isomorphism.

title: algebra-lemma-formally-etale-principal-parts
snippet: Let $R \to S \to S'$ be ring maps with $S \to S'$ formally \'etale (for example \'etale). Let $M$ be an $S$-module. Set $M' = S' \otimes_R M$. Then we have $$ S' \otimes_S P^k_{S/R}(M) = P^k_{S'/R}(M') $$ It follows that for any $S$-module $N$ and any finite order differential operator $D : M \to N$ there exists a unique extension $D' : M' \to S' \otimes_S N$ of $D$ to a differential operator (of the same or lesser order).

title: algebra-remark-formally-etale-differential-operators
snippet: Let $R \to S \to S'$ be ring maps with $S \to S'$ formally \'etale (for example \'etale). Let $M_i$, $i = 1, 2, 3$ be $S$-modules and let $D_i : M_i \to M_{i + 1}$, $i = 1, 2$ be differential operators of finite order. Then if $D'_i : M'_i \to M'_{i + 1}$, $i = 1, 2$ are the extensions of $D_i$ to $M'_i = S' \otimes_S M_i$ as in Lemma \ref{lemma-formally-etale-principal-parts}, then $D'_2 \circ D'_1$ is the extension of $D_2 \circ D_1$. In particular, if $M$ is an $S$-module, then $M' = S' \otimes_S M$ is a module over the $S$-algebra $\text{Diff}_{S/R}(M, M)$.

title: modules-lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation
snippet: Let $(X,\mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finitely presented $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ be a morphism of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. If $\mathcal{G}$ is finite type, then $\Coker(\varphi)$ is finitely presented.

title: modules-lemma-base-change-flat
snippet: Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed spaces. If $\mathcal{G}$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module, then $f^*\mathcal{G}$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

title: sites-modules-lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation
snippet: Let $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finitely presented $\mathcal{O}$-module. Let $\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ be a morphism of $\mathcal{O}$-modules. If $\mathcal{G}$ is finite type, then $\Coker(\varphi)$ is finitely presented.

title: cohomology-lemma-base-change-cup-product
snippet: Consider a commutative square $$ \xymatrix{ (X', \mathcal{O}_{X'}) \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \ar[d]^f \\ (Y', \mathcal{O}_{Y'}) \ar[r]^g & (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) } $$ of ringed spaces. Let $K, L$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. The relative cup product is compatible with the square in the sense that the diagram $$ \xymatrix{ Lg^*(Rf_*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^\mathbf{L} Rf_*L) \ar[r] \ar@{=}[d] & Lg^*(Rf_*(K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} L)) \ar[d] \\ Lg^*Rf_*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y'}}^\mathbf{L} Lg^*Rf_*L \ar[d] & R(f')_*L(g')^*(K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} L) \ar@{=}[d]…

title: sites-cohomology-lemma-base-change-cup-product
snippet: Consider a commutative square $$ \xymatrix{ (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'}) \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & (\Sh(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}}) \ar[d]^f \\ (\Sh(\mathcal{D}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'}) \ar[r]^g & (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}}) } $$ of ringed topoi. Let $K, L$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}})$.

title: properties-lemma-standard-open-two-affines
snippet: Let $U$, $V$ be affine schemes and let $W \to U$ and $W \to V$ be open immersions. For any $w \in W$ there exists an affine open neighbourhood $W' \subset W$ of $w$ such that $W'$ maps to a standard open of both $U$ and $V$.

title: derham-lemma-funny-map-functorial
snippet: Let $R_1 \to R_2$ be a ring homomorphism. For $i = 1, 2$ consider commutative diagrams $$ \xymatrix{ 0 \ar[r] & K_i^0 \ar[r] & L_i^0 \ar[r] & M_i^0 \ar[r] & 0 \\ & & L_i^{-1} \ar[u]_{\partial_i} \ar@{=}[r] & M_i^{-1} \ar[u] } $$ of $R_i$-modules as in Lemma \ref{lemma-funny-map}. Assume we have maps $K_1^0 \to K_2^0$, $L_1^j \to L_2^j$, $M_1^j \to M_2^j$ compatible with the given ring map $R_1 \to R_2$ and compatible with the maps in the displayed diagrams.

title: derham-lemma-base-change-Garel-upstairs
snippet: Consider a commutative diagram $$ \xymatrix{ Y' \ar[d]_{f'} \ar[r]_b & Y \ar[d]^f \\ X' \ar[r]^a & X } $$ of schemes which induces an isomorphism of $Y'$ with an open subscheme of $X' \times_X Y$. Assume $f$ is locally quasi-finite and syntomic and assume given maps $c^p_{Y/X} : \Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}} \to f^*\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} \det(\NL_{Y/X})$ for $p \geq 0$ satisfying (\ref{item-degree-zero}) and (\ref{item-multiplicative}).

title: derham-lemma-existence-base-change-Garel-upstairs
snippet: Consider a commutative diagram $$ \xymatrix{ Y' \ar[d]_{f'} \ar[r]_b & Y \ar[d]^f \\ X' \ar[r]^a & X } $$ of schemes which induces an isomorphism of $Y'$ with an open subscheme of $X' \times_X Y$. Assume $f$ is locally quasi-finite and syntomic. Then for every $y' \in Y'$ we can find opens $V' \subset Y'$, $V \subset Y$, $U' \subset X$, $U \subset X$ with $y' \in V'$, with $f'(V') \subset U'$, $b(V') \subset V$, $a(U') \subset U$, $f(V) \subset U$, and such that for $p \geq 0$ there are maps $c^p_{V/U}$ and $c^p_{V'/U'}$ satisfying (\ref{item-degree-zero}) and (\ref{item-multiplicative})…

title: algebra-lemma-base-change-along-universally-injective-ring-map
snippet: Let $R \to S$ be a ring map which is universally injective as a map of $R$-modules. Then the functor $M \mapsto M \otimes_R S$ on $R$-modules reflects injections, surjections, and isomorphisms.

title: derived-remark-functoriality-derived-limit
snippet: Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category. Let $(K_n)$ and $(L_n)$ be inverse systems of objects of $\mathcal{D}$ with derived limits $K$ and $L$. Suppose we have a morphism $a : (K_n) \to (L_n)$ of pro-objects, see Categories, Example \ref{categories-example-pro-morphism-inverse-systems}. This means we are given maps $a_n : K_{m(n)} \to L_n$. We may assume $m(1) < m(2) < m(3) < \ldots$ and that the maps $a_n$ are compatible with the transition maps in the systems.

title: more-algebra-lemma-pro-isomorphism-iso-Rlim
snippet: Let $(A_n)$ and $(B_n)$ be inverse systems of abelian groups. A morphism of pro-systems $\varphi : (A_n) \to (B_n)$ determines maps $\lim A_n \to \lim B_n$ and $R^1\lim A_n \to R^1\lim B_n$. These maps are isomorphisms if $\varphi$ is a pro-isomorphism.

title: more-algebra-lemma-pro-isomorphism-Rlim
snippet: Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category. Let $(K_n)$ and $(M_n)$ be inverse systems of objects of $\mathcal{D}$ with derived limits $K$ and $M$. Let $a : (K_n) \to (M_n)$ be a pro-isomorphism of pro-objects. Then $a$ can be used to produce a (non-canonical) isomorphism $K \to M$.

title: algebra-remark-local-ring-fibre
snippet: Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ lying over the prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$. According to Remark \ref{remark-fundamental-diagram} the prime $\mathfrak q$ corresponds to a unique prime $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ of the fibre ring $F = S \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

title: homology-remark-idempotent-symmetry
snippet: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category, $x$ an object of $\mathcal{A}$, and $f : x \to x$ idempotent. Writing $g = \text{id} _ x - f$, one has $f \circ g = 0$, $g \circ f = 0$, and $g \circ g = g$.

title: homology-lemma-idempotent-kernel-cokernel
snippet: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category, $x$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$, and $f : x \to x$ be idempotent. Write $g = \text{id} _ x - f$ and recall by Remark \ref{remark-idempotent-symmetry} that $f \circ g = g \circ f = 0$. \begin{enumerate} \item If $f$ has kernel $i : \Ker (f) \to x$ and $p$ is the unique morphism such that $g = i \circ p$, then $p \circ i = \text{id} _ {\Ker (f)}$ and $p$ is the cokernel of $f$.

title: homology-lemma-idempotent-splitting
snippet: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category, $x$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$, and $f : x \to x$ be idempotent. Write $g = \text{id} _ x - f$. If each of $f$ and $g$ have at least one of a kernel or cokernel and in turn morphisms $i , j , p , q$ are constructed as in the statement of Lemma \ref{lemma-idempotent-kernel-cokernel}, then all four (co)kernels exist and \begin{align*} x & \simeq \Ker (f) \oplus \Ker (g) \\ & \simeq \Coker (f) \oplus \Ker (g) \\ & \simeq \Ker (f) \oplus \Coker (g) \\ & \simeq \Coker (f) \oplus \Coker (g) \end{align*} with the structure of each direct product given…

title: homology-lemma-split-morphism-kernel-cokernel
snippet: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category, $x$ and $y$ be objects of $\mathcal{A}$, and $j : y \to x$ and $q : x \to y$ be morphisms satisfying $q \circ j = \text{id} _ y$. Then \begin{enumerate} \item $\text{id} _ x - j \circ q$ has kernel $j$. \item $\text{id} _ x - j \circ q$ has cokernel $q$. \end{enumerate}

title: homology-lemma-split-morphism-splitting
snippet: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category, $x$ and $y$ be objects of $\mathcal{A}$, and $j : y \to x$ and $q : x \to y$ be morphisms satisfying $q \circ j = \text{id} _ y$. If $j \circ q$ has at least one of a kernel or cokernel, then both (co)kernels exist and \begin{align*} x & \simeq \Ker (j \circ q) \oplus y \\ & \simeq \Coker (j \circ q) \oplus y \end{align*} with the structure of either direct product including $j , q$, and the canonical (co)kernel morphism, and the remaining map uniquely determined.

title: more-algebra-definition-rank
snippet: Let $R$ be a domain with fraction field $K$. The {\it rank} of an $R$-module $M$ is $\dim_K(M \otimes_R K)$.

title: more-algebra-lemma-torsion-does-not-matter-rank
snippet: Let $R$ be a domain. If $M \to M'$ is a map of $R$-modules whose kernel and cokernel are torsion, then the rank of $M$ equals the rank of $M'$.

title: more-algebra-lemma-rank-additive
snippet: Let $R$ be a domain. Let $0 \to M \to M' \to M'' \to 0$ be a short exact sequence of $R$-modules. Then the rank of $M'$ is the sum of the ranks of $M$ and $M''$.

title: more-algebra-lemma-rank-tensor
snippet: Let $R$ be a domain. Let $M$ and $N$ be $R$-modules. \begin{enumerate} \item The rank of $M \otimes_R N$ is the product of the ranks of $M$ and $N$. \item If $M$ is a finitely presented $R$-module, then the rank of $\Hom_R(M, N)$ is the product of the ranks of $M$ and $N$. \end{enumerate}

title: more-algebra-lemma-dominant-pullback-rank
snippet: Let $R \subset R'$ be an extension of domains. If $M$ is an $R$-module, then the rank of $M$ over $R$ is equal to the rank of $M \otimes_R R'$ over $R'$.

title: more-algebra-lemma-finite-module-rank
snippet: Let $R$ be a domain. Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module. Then \begin{enumerate} \item $M$ has finite rank $r \geq 0$, \item there is a map $M \to R^{\oplus r}$ whose kernel and cokernel are torsion modules, \item there is an $f \in R$, $f \not = 0$ such that $M_f$ is free of rank $r$, and \item there is an injective map $R^{\oplus r} \to M$ whose cokernel is a torsion module. \end{enumerate}

title: more-algebra-example-counter-description-P
snippet: The equality in (6) of Lemma \ref{lemma-galois-inertia} is false without the assumption on $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$. A counterexample is the extension of $A = Z_2[t]_{(2)}$ given by $B = A[x]/(x^2 - t)$. Namely then $\sigma(x) = -x = x - 2x$ and $2x$ is not in $\mathfrak m^2$.

title: schemes-lemma-local-ring-fibre
snippet: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$. Thinking of $x$ as a point of $X_s$ (see Lemma \ref{lemma-fibre-topological}) we have $$ \mathcal{O}_{X_s, x} \cong \mathcal{O}_{X, x}/\mathfrak m_s\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \cong \mathcal{O}_{X, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S, s}} \kappa(s) $$

title: properties-definition-G-scheme
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme. We say $X$ is a {\it G-scheme}\footnote{This may be nonstandard terminology. If $G$ is a finite group or group scheme then sometimes a $G$-scheme denotes a scheme equipped with an action of $G$.} if for every $x \in X$ there exists an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is a G-ring (see More on Algebra, Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-G-ring}).

title: properties-lemma-characterize-G-scheme
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $X$ is a G-scheme, \item $X$ is locally Noetherian and for all $x \in X$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}^\wedge$ is regular, and \item $X$ is locally Noetherian and for any closed point $x \in X$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}^\wedge$ is regular. \end{enumerate}

title: properties-lemma-locally-G-scheme
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item The scheme $X$ is a G-scheme. \item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is a G-ring. \item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is a G-ring. \item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$ such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is a G-scheme. \end{enumerate} Moreover, if $X$ is a G-scheme then every open subscheme is a G-scheme.

title: morphisms-definition-excellent
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme. \begin{enumerate} \item We say $X$ is {\it quasi-excellent} if for every $x \in X$ there exists an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is quasi-excellent (see More on Algebra, Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-excellent}). \item We say $X$ is {\it excellent} if for every $x \in X$ there exists an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is excellent (see More on Algebra, Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-excellent}). \end{enumerate}

title: morphisms-lemma-characterize-quasi-excellent
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent \begin{enumerate} \item $X$ is quasi-excellent, and \item $X$ is a G-scheme and J-2. \end{enumerate}

title: morphisms-lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata
snippet: A quasi-excellent scheme is Nagata.

title: morphisms-lemma-characterize-excellent
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent \begin{enumerate} \item $X$ is excellent, and \item $X$ is quasi-excellent and universally catenary. \end{enumerate}

title: morphisms-lemma-locally-excellent
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item The scheme $X$ is (quasi-)excellent. \item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is (quasi-)excellent. \item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is (quasi-)excellent. \item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$ such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is (quasi-)excellent. \end{enumerate} Moreover, if $X$ is (quasi-)excellent then every open subscheme is (quasi-)excellent.

title: morphisms-lemma-finite-type-excellent
snippet: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism. If $S$ is (quasi-)excellent and $f$ locally of finite type then $X$ is (quasi-)excellent.

title: morphisms-lemma-ubiquity-excellent
snippet: The following types of schemes are excellent. \begin{enumerate} \item Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. \item Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian complete local ring. \item Any scheme locally of finite type over $\mathbf{Z}$. \item Any scheme locally of finite type over a Dedekind ring of characteristic zero. \end{enumerate}

title: divisors-definition-rank
snippet: Let $X$ be an integral scheme with generic point $\eta$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. The {\it rank} of $\mathcal{F}$ is $\dim_{\kappa(\eta)} \mathcal{F}_\eta$.

title: divisors-lemma-check-rank-on-affines
snippet: Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $r$ be a cardinal. The following are equivalent \begin{enumerate} \item $\mathcal{F}$ has rank $r$, \item for all $U \subset X$ nonempty affine open $\mathcal{F}(U)$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$-module of rank $r$, and \item for some $U \subset X$ nonempty affine open $\mathcal{F}(U)$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$-module of rank $r$. \end{enumerate}

title: divisors-lemma-dominant-pullback-rank
snippet: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a dominant morphism of integral schemes. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module. Then the rank of $\mathcal{G}$ on $Y$ is equal to the rank of $f^*\mathcal{G}$ on $X$.

title: divisors-lemma-rank-additive
snippet: Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{F}'' \to 0$ be a short exact sequence of quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Then the rank of $\mathcal{F}'$ is the sum of the ranks of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}''$.

title: divisors-lemma-rank-tensor
snippet: Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. \begin{enumerate} \item The rank of $\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{G}$ is the product of the ranks of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$. \item If $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation, then the rank of $\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$ is the product of the ranks of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$. \end{enumerate}

title: divisors-lemma-finite-module-rank
snippet: Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then \begin{enumerate} \item $\mathcal{F}$ has finite rank $r \geq 0$, and \item there exists a nonempty open $U \subset X$ such that $\mathcal{F}|_U$ is free of rank $r$. \end{enumerate}

title: more-morphisms-lemma-formally-unramified
snippet: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $f$ is formally unramified, \item for every $x \in X$ there exist opens $x \in U \subset X$ and $f(x) \in V \subset Y$ with $f(U) \subset V$ such that $f|_U : U \to V$ is formally unramified, \item for every pair of affine opens $U \subset X$ and $V \subset Y$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_Y(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is formally unramified, and \item there exists an affine open covering $Y = \bigcup V_j$ and for each $j$ an affine open covering $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup U_{ji}$ such…

title: more-morphisms-lemma-formally-etale
snippet: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $f$ is formally \'etale, \item for every $x \in X$ there exist opens $x \in U \subset X$ and $f(x) \in V \subset Y$ with $f(U) \subset V$ such that $f|_U : U \to V$ is formally \'etale, \item for every pair of affine opens $U \subset X$ and $V \subset Y$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_Y(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is formally \'etale, and \item there exists an affine open covering $Y = \bigcup V_j$ and for each $j$ an affine open covering $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup U_{ji}$ such that…

title: etale-cohomology-lemma-F-2
snippet: In the situation of Lemma \ref{lemma-F-1} let $k'/k$ be an extension of algebraically closed fields. Set $V' = V \otimes_k k'$ and $F' : V' \to V'$ be the Frobenius linear map induced by $F$. Then $\Ker(F - 1)$ maps isomorphically onto $\Ker(F' - 1)$.

title: spaces-cohomology-lemma-etale-pull-push-split
snippet: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact, separated, \'etale morphism of algebraic spaces. Then for any quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ the map $f^*f_*\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$ is split.

title: examples-lemma-etale-not-dominated-zariski-finite-etale
snippet: The \'etale cover $U \to X$ cannot be refined by any finite composition of open immersions and finite \'etale morphisms.

title: examples-lemma-nonfinite-h0
snippet: Non-finite $H^0$. \begin{enumerate} \item There exists a ring $R$ and a projective scheme $X$ over $R$ such that $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is not a finite $R$-module. \item There exists a ring $R$ and a finite type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbf{P}^1_R$ such that $H^0(\mathbf{P}^1_R, \mathcal{F})$ is not a finite $R$-module. \end{enumerate}
